messages:
sam: Heads-up — spike in small-model traffic this morning, and org-level quotas hit. Thinking we need a per-model-slab quota + burst pool to avoid killing low-priority jobs. Anyone object to adding model-size buckets (tiny/small/medium/large) on top of org/key quotas?
anya: +1 for slabs. We saw this with image-captioning too — all single-token calls blow through generic quota. Model-family granularity would help.
mike: question: where do we enforce? edge gateway (fast but duplicated), router (centralized but slower), or runtime (accurate per-GPU accounting)?
keisha: my vote is router-level enforcement with token-credit sync to runtime. Router can cheaply reject/fallback before queuing. Runtime should be the source of truth for usage report.
lucas: can we support burst tokens that draw from org pool first, then slab pool? e.g., org has 1k/sec, slab gets additional 200 token bursts for short periods.
anya: yeah — two-tier: steady-state rate by org/key + eligible burst caps per model-slab. Bursts should decay with time-window and be refillable.
quota-bot: note: current per-key rate-limit header: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 482, X-RateLimit-Reset: 1670000000. No slab info today.
mike: UX concern: console needs to show per-model consumption and burst budget in realtime. Product asked for a compact view per-route too.
keisha: draft of enforcement config I sketched:
```json
{
  "quota_policy": {
    "org_quota": { "rate_per_min": 60000 },
    "slabs": {
      "tiny": { "rate_per_min": 20000, "burst": 500 },
      "small": { "rate_per_min": 15000, "burst": 300 },
      "medium": { "rate_per_min": 10000, "burst": 200 },
      "large": { "rate_per_min": 5000, "burst": 50 }
    },
    "fallback_policy": { "on_quota_exhaust": "route-to-smaller-compatible" }
  }
}
```
sam: Love the fallback_policy idea. We can automatically route to a smaller model family when slab quota exhausted, with option for 429 if the caller opts out.
anya: telemetry events to emit: quota.check (allowed/denied), burst.draw, slab.switch. Need distinct metrics to track how often fallback routing is used so we can tune defaults.
lucas: will need labels: org_id, key_id, slab, model_family, route, tokens_consumed, reason. Also include request_latency and queued_time for cost analysis.
mike: Implementation plan:
- router: enforce steady-state + fast burst counters (in-memory + redis fallback)
- runtime: authoritative accounting and reconciler job every minute
- console: per-org -> per-slab dashboard + alert when slab usage > 80% for 5m
- API: expose headers X-Slab-Remaining, X-Slab-Burst-Remaining, X-Fallback-Applied
keisha: also add a per-model-size cost_multiplier so billing and quotas align (e.g., medium consumes 1.5x tokens for quota accounting vs tiny).
sam: quick compatibility question — how do we define model->slab mapping? static manifest or dynamic based on params (seq_len, weights)?
anya: start with a curated manifest (model id -> slab) maintained in model-catalog. Could add runtime heuristics later.
quota-bot: action created: QUOTA-213 add slab quotas + burst pool prototypes. Assigned to @keisha.
deploy-bot: deploy completed: router/quota-proto v0.1 -> staging at 1765559925
mike: tested staging: burst draw works, but saw ~0.5% race where two concurrent requests both passed router check and runtime later reconciled one as overdrawn. Need better atomic increment semantics (redis lua or token-bucket in single store).
keisha: ack. I'll swap to redis lua script for atomic draw and add a compensating reconciler to refund misdraws to slab pool.
sam: ok plan. next: let's pin telemetry event names and console mock. Can we sketch a tiny UI widget for product?
anya: will put a mock in Figma and share a link later. For now, I'll create a minimal console wireframe: per-org header, slab breakdown bar with hover shows burst remaining + last refill time.
lucas: also add audit trail entries when fallback routing modifies request target (for security/compliance).
mike: sounds good. If no blockers I'll mark QUOTA-213 as in-progress and we can ramp in canary tenants.
sam: thanks all — please drop PR when proto tests green. :thumbsup:
